chunks.title: Pathfinder Second Edition Remaster core rules reference
chunks.text:
# Pathfinder Second Edition Remaster core rules reference

This reference is a compact, rules-focused aid for the AIGM. It summarizes the open core procedures used most often during play. A character record remains the authority for that character's exact feats, spells, items, and class abilities.

chunks.title: Core check
chunks.text:
## Core check
Roll 1d20 and add the relevant modifier. Compare the total with the Difficulty Class. A total equal to or higher than the DC succeeds.

Pathfinder uses four degrees of success. A result at least 10 above the DC is a critical success. A result at least 10 below the DC is a critical failure. A natural 20 improves the degree of success by one step. A natural 1 worsens it by one step.

chunks.title: Proficiency
chunks.text:
## Proficiency
A proficiency modifier normally includes the character's level plus a rank bonus: trained adds level + 2, expert level + 4, master level + 6, and legendary level + 8. An untrained check normally adds no proficiency bonus unless a rule says otherwise.

Use the exact modifier printed on the character record when it is available. Do not rebuild the modifier unless the player asks for an audit.

chunks.title: Encounter turns
chunks.text:
## Encounter turns
At the start of an encounter, roll initiative. Perception is the normal initiative skill, but another skill may be used when it fits what the character was doing before the encounter.

On a turn, a creature normally has three actions and one reaction. Activities may cost one, two, or three actions. Free actions do not consume the three-action allowance. A reaction can be used only when its trigger occurs.

Do not import D&D's action, bonus-action, and movement structure into Pathfinder Second Edition.

chunks.title: Multiple attacks
chunks.text:
## Multiple attacks
Each attack with the attack trait contributes to the multiple attack penalty. The normal penalty is -5 on the second attack and -10 on later attacks during the same turn. Agile attacks normally use -4 and -8 instead. Apply any printed character feature that changes these values.

chunks.title: Basic saving throws
chunks.text:
## Basic saving throws
For a basic Fortitude, Reflex, or Will save: critical success means no damage, success means half damage, failure means full damage, and critical failure means double damage. Specific effects can replace this pattern.

chunks.title: Armor Class and attacks
chunks.text:
## Armor Class and attacks
An attack roll is normally compared with Armor Class. A critical success normally doubles the damage rather than requiring a separate confirmation roll. Do not use Pathfinder First Edition's critical-threat confirmation procedure.

chunks.title: Movement
chunks.text:
## Movement
Stride moves up to Speed. Step moves 5 feet and usually avoids reactions triggered by movement. Difficult terrain costs extra movement. Forced movement is not voluntary movement and follows the effect that caused it.

chunks.title: Perception and detection
chunks.text:
## Perception and detection
Perception is used for initiative, noticing creatures and details, and Sense Motive. Sense Motive is a Perception action used to judge whether behavior seems deceptive; it is not the skill used to steal an item.

Observed, hidden, undetected, and unnoticed describe how well a creature is detected. Concealed normally requires a flat check to target. Hidden targets usually require a harder flat check and are off-guard to the observer. Use the current rules text or supplied effect when an exact flat-check DC matters.

chunks.title: Stealth
chunks.text:
## Stealth
Avoid Notice is an exploration activity. Hide and Sneak are encounter actions. Hiding generally requires cover or concealment. Sneak moves while trying to remain undetected. Compare Stealth with the observers' Perception DCs unless a specific rule calls for a roll.

chunks.title: Thievery
chunks.text:
## Thievery
Thievery covers stealing, disabling devices, picking locks, and related manual tricks. To lift an item from a creature, use the Steal action and a Thievery check against the target's Perception DC, subject to the action's limits and the circumstances.

Do not call for Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) in Pathfinder Second Edition. That is neighboring-edition terminology.

chunks.title: Common skill actions
chunks.text:
## Common skill actions
Athletics includes maneuvers such as Grapple, Reposition, Shove, and Trip. Acrobatics includes Balance, Escape in appropriate cases, Maneuver in Flight, and Tumble Through. Deception includes Create a Diversion, Feint, Impersonate, and Lie. Diplomacy includes Gather Information, Make an Impression, and Request. Intimidation includes Coerce and Demoralize. Medicine includes Administer First Aid and Treat Wounds. Recall Knowledge uses the skill appropriate to the subject.

Use the named action when it matters, but keep play moving when the intent is clear. Ask for the relevant printed skill modifier rather than converting the action to a D&D ability check.

chunks.title: Aid
chunks.text:
## Aid
A creature can prepare to help and then use a reaction when the trigger occurs. The GM chooses an appropriate skill or attack roll and DC. The degree of success determines the bonus or penalty. Use the current printed Aid values if the exact bonus is important.

chunks.title: Cover and off-guard
chunks.text:
## Cover and off-guard
Cover improves defenses according to its degree. Lesser cover and standard cover are distinct. A creature may be off-guard because it is flanked, hidden from the attacker, affected by a condition, or subject to another rule. Off-guard normally imposes a -2 circumstance penalty to AC.

chunks.title: Flanking
chunks.text:
## Flanking
Two creatures flank an enemy when they are on substantially opposite sides, can act, can attack, and meet the reach requirements. A flanked creature is normally off-guard to the flankers.

chunks.title: Conditions
chunks.text:
## Conditions
Frightened applies a status penalty equal to its value to checks and DCs and usually decreases by 1 at the end of the creature's turn. Sickened applies a status penalty and normally requires retching to reduce. Clumsy penalizes Dexterity-based checks and DCs, including AC. Enfeebled penalizes Strength-based checks and DCs. Stupefied penalizes Intelligence-, Wisdom-, and Charisma-based checks and DCs and can disrupt spellcasting. Drained reduces Constitution-related durability and maximum Hit Points. Slowed reduces available actions. Quickened adds an action with limits set by the effect. Stunned removes actions. Immobilized prevents move actions that change position. Restrained is more severe than grabbed. Persistent damage is rolled at the end of the turn followed by a flat check to end it.

Use the exact condition value and duration supplied by the effect. Conditions of the same type generally do not stack; use the highest value unless a rule says otherwise.

chunks.title: Hit Points, dying, and wounded
chunks.text:
## Hit Points, dying, and wounded
At 0 Hit Points, a creature normally falls unconscious and gains dying. The dying value is usually 1, or 2 if the effect that dropped the creature was a critical success or came from a critical failure. Add the wounded value when gaining dying.

At the start of the creature's turn, attempt a recovery check with a DC based on the dying value. A success reduces dying by 1, a critical success by 2, a failure increases dying by 1, and a critical failure by 2. Dying 4 normally means death. Taking damage while dying increases the dying value.

When a creature loses dying and remains at 0 Hit Points, it is usually unconscious and wounded 1, or increases its wounded value. Healing that raises it above 0 Hit Points ends dying. Follow specific features that change these rules.

chunks.title: Hero Points
chunks.text:
## Hero Points
A player normally begins a session with at least one Hero Point and can gain more during play, subject to the campaign's handling. A Hero Point can reroll a check and use the second result. Spending all Hero Points can prevent death when dying would otherwise reach the fatal threshold, following the current rule.

chunks.title: Healing and Treat Wounds
chunks.text:
## Healing and Treat Wounds
Magical and mundane healing restore Hit Points as stated. Treat Wounds is a Medicine activity that takes time, uses a DC tied to the attempted proficiency tier, and normally creates temporary immunity to further Treat Wounds. Battle Medicine is a separate feat-based combat option.

chunks.title: Spells
chunks.text:
## Spells
Spell attacks are attack rolls and can suffer the multiple attack penalty. Saving-throw spells use the caster's spell DC. Many spells use four degrees of success. Sustain a Spell normally costs one action each round when required. Concentration is a trait in Pathfinder Second Edition, not D&D's one-concentration-spell subsystem.

Prepared and spontaneous spellcasters follow the exact entries on the character record. Do not invent spell slots, focus points, traditions, or heightened effects.

chunks.title: Counteract
chunks.text:
## Counteract
Counteracting compares a counteract check with the target DC and uses counteract ranks to determine which effects can be ended. When the exact rank interaction matters, retrieve the specific rule or ask the player for the effect details rather than importing D&D's counterspell procedure.

chunks.title: Exploration mode
chunks.text:
## Exploration mode
Exploration activities describe what characters do while moving through the world: Avoid Notice, Defend, Detect Magic, Follow the Expert, Hustle, Investigate, Repeat a Spell, Scout, Search, and others. A character generally concentrates on one exploration activity at a time unless a feature says otherwise.

chunks.title: Downtime mode
chunks.text:
## Downtime mode
Downtime covers activities measured in days, such as Earn Income, Craft, retrain, recover, and pursue long projects. Use the appropriate skill and the settlement or task level when the exact result matters.

chunks.title: Encounter difficulty
chunks.text:
## Encounter difficulty
Pathfinder encounter budgets depend on party level, party size, and creature levels. Do not estimate solely from D&D challenge ratings. When exact encounter math is unavailable, favor conservative opposition and adjust using the campaign's danger preference.

chunks.title: Character agency
chunks.text:
## Character agency
A personality entry, ideal, flaw, alignment, anathema, edict, or backstory note informs roleplay but does not let the Game Master choose a player-character's voluntary action. The Game Master may point out an apparent conflict when useful, then let the player decide.

chunks.title: Edition boundary
chunks.text:
## Edition boundary
Use Pathfinder Second Edition Remaster vocabulary and procedures. Do not silently substitute D&D 5e, D&D 3.5e, or Pathfinder First Edition mechanics. When the stored reference and character record do not answer a question, make a clear temporary ruling and say that it is a ruling rather than quoting a rule that was not found.
